label: Badge
title: Badge
summary: Use a Badge to make a short status, category, or count easy to scan beside the content it describes.
corePrinciple: Say one thing, in a few words. Let the label carry the meaning and use emphasis to establish priority.

anatomy.title: A compact signal
anatomy.description: A leading cue, short label, and token-owned surface form one compact message.
blocks: Adds a recognizable cue without replacing the words.
Groups the message into one compact shape.

anatomy.note: Adds a recognizable cue without replacing the words.
Groups the message into one compact shape.

configuration.title: Choose treatment and meaning
configuration.description: Use a solid Badge beside ordinary content. Use glass where the underlying image or surface remains part of the composition.

states.title: Content, action, and loading
states.description: Most badges communicate information. Add an action only when opening related detail is useful. Loading shows that the value is still arriving.

sizing.title: Content determines the width
sizing.description: Choose the size for the surrounding density. Keep the label short so the Badge remains a compact companion.

content.title: Write the status, not a sentence
content.description: Use familiar words. Keep tense and capitalization consistent across the same set.

inContext.title: Keep status beside its subject
inContext.description: Place the compact status next to the item it describes.

doDont.title: Make status clear at a glance
doDont.description: Keep labels concise, match their meaning, and establish a clear priority.
blocks: Avoid a sentence inside the Badge
Avoid putting the whole explanation inside the Badge.
Use semantic treatment that agrees with the status.
Conflicting words and tone make the status harder to trust.
Give the status needing attention the strongest emphasis.
If every status competes, the urgent one is harder to find.
Keep comparable statuses similar in length and capitalization.
Mixed wording and capitalization slow scanning.
